text:
Muse (Meta) endpoint 400s on oneOf — switch tool schemas to anyOf

Symptom (observed 2027-01-18, live in-session): a streaming request to the Meta "muse" endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/chat/completions) failed terminally — HTTP 400 {"error":{"code":null,"message":"'oneOf' is not permitted.","param":"parameters","type":"invalid_request_error"}}. Retries exhausted; the agent turn died. Reproduce: on the muse endpoint, run any turn whose request includes the create_plan/update_plan tools — their `steps` items schema embeds a oneOf union, and muse's OpenAI-compat layer rejects `oneOf` outright inside tool `parameters`.

Exact sites:
- src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:703 — create_plan steps.items.oneOf [string | {header, body}]
- src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:1116 — update_plan steps.items.oneOf (same shape)
- src/tool/mod.rs:1475 — test stringified_null_dropped_through_union_branches mirrors that schema (update in lockstep)
- Request path: src/provider/openai.rs:691 (the "stream request" provider_error). Walkers that must stay consistent: src/tool/mod.rs:222 and :235 (drop_stringified_nulls recurses into anyOf/oneOf/allOf) and src/provider/strict.rs:59/:87/:208 (strict-mode normalizer already walks anyOf branches).

Fix direction (user-confirmed 2027-01-18): use anyOf instead of oneOf — replace both hand-written oneOf unions with anyOf at the two plan.rs sites and mirror the change in the tool/mod.rs test schema. Semantics: these are permissive unions (a step is a string OR an object), so anyOf is the correct, looser match; oneOf's exactly-one constraint was never intended.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A search for oneOf in src/ returns only walker KEY lists (src/tool/mod.rs:235, src/provider/strict.rs:87/:208) — no emitted tool schema carries it.
2. Regression test: build the create_plan (and update_plan) tool schema and assert the serialized `parameters` contain "anyOf" and no "oneOf".
3. The strict-mode and drop_stringified_nulls tests still pass (anyOf flows through both walkers unchanged).
4. cargo test green (workspace).
5. Manual: a muse turn including create_plan/update_plan no longer 400s.

Pointers: error-string precedent src/error.rs:388-429 (provider_error shape); failure observed in the job-3b session (2027-01-18 harness note).

text:
Close the 340K proxy-cache cliff leak (R20a-c)

Problem (2027-01-09 cache round 5, HIGH): post-R12, 47 requests still crossed the ~340K litellm proxy cache ceiling at 16.3% hit (340-400K bucket: 83.7% resets; daily maxP reaches 408,956). R13 (fill_rate 0.3 + the 340K ceiling minus a 32,768 margin → effective trigger ~300K on 1M-window GLM endpoints) did NOT prevent over-cliff prompts.

Root cause (three stacked gaps, code-verified):
1. Rule-4 skip: when the conversation ends in an open tool loop spanning back to messages[1] (a long single-turn tool run — exactly where context grows fastest), summary_cut_index retreats the cut to the loop start and summarize returns messages UNCHANGED (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338, 437-485); maybe_compact falls through and the request is sent at full size.
2. No send-gate: when compaction runs but cannot shrink below the threshold, the code explicitly continues (src/agent/turn.rs:1743-1750 — "Still over: the kept-verbatim tail dominates..."); the 5-attempt budget aborts only on the 5th attempt, so up to 4 over-cliff requests go out per turn, and the next turn resets the budget.
3. Tokenizer drift: the trigger counts cl100k BPE tokens; the provider counts GLM tokens (~10% higher on code-heavy content) — a 300K-cl100k conversation can be 330-345K provider tokens, and one iteration's tool results plus GLM reasoning echo (policy: never strip) jumps past the trigger between checks.

Fix instructions (R20, three parts):
a. Send-gate at the cliff (src/agent/turn.rs maybe_compact ~:1660-1760): when the pre-request count is still over the proxy ceiling after the compaction attempts, do NOT send the full prompt — either (i) allow under-pressure historical-reasoning stripping for GLM as a cliff-pressure exception (the under_pressure machinery exists at src/provider/openai/request.rs:54 and DeepSeek uses it; GLM's never-strip policy blocks it — src/provider/policy.rs), or (ii) fail the turn fast with an actionable error instead of burning up to 4 over-cliff requests.
b. Trigger margin for 1M-window endpoints (src/config/general.rs:334/343 defaults; src/agent/context.rs:151-163 trigger math): lower the effective trigger to ~280K (fill 0.28 for 1M windows, or ceiling 320K) so tokenizer drift plus one tool batch cannot jump past the cliff.
c. Rule-4 fast-fail signal: when summarize no-ops because the open tool loop spans the conversation AND the count is over the ceiling, return a "skipped: open loop" signal from summarize/summarize_with_interrupt (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338) so maybe_compact surfaces "context over the proxy cache ceiling inside an open tool loop — finish or interrupt the tool run" immediately instead of silently re-sending.

Acceptance: a regression test where a conversation over the ceiling inside an open tool loop fails fast (or strips under pressure) instead of sending >340K; no post-fix request_stats row exceeds the ceiling (verify via the aggregates extraction); cargo test --workspace green with the existing compaction tests updated to the new behavior.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-cache-hit-5-review.md (HIGH-1, R20); .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt (A3/A4 buckets); executive summary BUG 4.

Fix run-all dispatch writing the plan link onto the previous backlog item

Bug 69093a21 (observed 2027-01-11, run-all batch; reproduced twice in one session): when run-all dispatches the next item, the plan link (plan_id + plan_title) is written onto the WRONG record in .coding/backlog.jsonl — always the same stale item a25a5323 (budget), while the actually-dispatched item stayed in Pending with no link. Observation 1: budget item a25a5323's plan a1047bff completed, next item 627ee5d9 (plan 07ff4ea6) dispatched -> a25a5323 gained plan_id 07ff4ea6. Observation 2: 627ee5d9 closed, 6e071b07 (plan f0758c0d) dispatched -> a25a5323 was overwritten with f0758c0d while 6e071b07 stayed Pending. Repro: run two back-to-back run-all items and diff backlog.jsonl after the second create_plan: git diff HEAD -- .coding/backlog.jsonl.

Impact: batch bookkeeping can re-dispatch a finished item or stall (a completed item reads InFlight); the stale plan link cannot be cleared with backlog_status (no plan-id setter), so a25a5323 still carries the wrong plan_id/plan_title.

Fix direction: src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs::stamp_backlog_in_flight (lines 7330-7376) resolves its target via a pointer fallback chain (pointer.or_else(|| chat_linkage_candidate(&store.items(), top_plan_id))) and then writes BacklogStore::set_plan_id (src/backlog.rs:703-723). The resolution must not overwrite a previously dispatched item's record — target the item just dispatched (by id/title) and stop trusting a stale link. Compare the agent-scoped refresh at run_all.rs:5444-5446, which targets by agent_id and looks correct by construction. Full detail: .coding/knowledge/bug/2027-01-11-run-all-dispatch-wrote-the-new-plan-link-onto-th.md (amended with both observations).

Acceptance: two back-to-back run-all dispatches leave each item carrying its OWN plan link; add a regression test on the dispatch/linkage path; cargo test run_all stays green.

text:
Image tools hidden in Planning and Complete

The image_* family (image_analysis, image_ui_diff, image_diff, ...) is invisible in the Planning and Complete workflow states, but those tools are READ-ONLY w.r.t. the project and are needed while planning — e.g. a plan that must account for an attached screenshot or design mockup cannot look at the image before a plan exists.

SYMPTOM (how to reproduce): from Complete or Planning, the tool list carries no image_* entry. Root cause, verified by reading the code: src/tool/mod.rs ToolFilter::allows() — the Planning arm (line ~583) and the Complete arm (line ~807) both gate ToolCategory::Agent to `(safety == SafetyLevel::AutoRun && !name.starts_with("mcp__")) || name == "spawn_agent"`. Every image tool in src/tool/agent/image_tools/tools.rs is ToolCategory::Agent (tools.rs:700, the ImageAnalysisTool impl) and reports `fn safety(&self) -> SafetyLevel { SafetyLevel::NeedsApproval }` (tools.rs:718), so both arms deny it. The family never mutates project files — it reads an image and calls the vision model — so the "no changes without a plan" rule does not justify hiding it; only the approval prompt does, and that prompt is orthogonal to state visibility (exactly the argument the Browser tools use at src/tool/mod.rs:615-622 and 811-817). Each image tool also sets `fn deferred_group(&self) -> Option<&'static str> { Some("image") }` (tools.rs:706), so the family is already tagged.

FIX DIRECTION (plan it): make the image family visible in Planning + Complete. Minimal, in-style option: name-gate the family in BOTH Agent arms of ToolFilter::allows() the same way spawn_agent already is — `|| name.starts_with("image_")` in the Planning arm (~line 583) and the Complete arm (~line 807). KEEP SafetyLevel::NeedsApproval so each call still prompts; do NOT relax the safety level to AutoRun, which would silently drop the approval prompt in Executing too. Alternative if name-matching the family is unwanted: add a trait-level read-only marker on Tool (e.g. `fn reads_only_project(&self) -> bool` defaulting to false) and consult it in both arms — prefer whichever option can be covered by a test that enumerates the REAL registered tool list rather than a hardcoded name list. Do not change the Reviewer or Skill arm behaviour.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) a test in src/tool/mod.rs beside the existing per-state availability tests (~lines 2316-2440, e.g. skill_create_is_executing_only_unless_a_skill_names_it) asserting every registered image_* tool is allowed under ToolFilter::Planning AND ToolFilter::Complete, while mutating Agent tools (file_edit, file_write, shell, git) stay DENIED in those two states — the plan-first hard rule must survive; (2) `cargo test` green and warning-free (the crate roots are #![deny(warnings)]); (3) if the Planning/Complete tool surface is described in docs/FEATURES.md or agent.md, update that text.

VERIFY: `cargo test` unpiped and read its result lines (never trust a piped exit code). Then confirm in-app that from Complete the image tools appear and that each call still prompts for approval.

POINTERS: the module doc is src/tool/agent/image_tools/mod.rs ("the image_* family, mirroring the vision-mcp spec"); the per-state availability test conventions live in src/tool/mod.rs tests (~2316-2440). Deletion hygiene: pre-flight import-orphan check before the battery

Under #![deny(warnings)] (both crate roots) each orphan is a hard build failure — two full cargo cycles were burned on a mechanically predictable failure. Fix direction: land the discipline where edits are governed — amend the project constitution's Code style section (agent.md at the repo root, "## Code style") with a deletion-hygiene rule: after any deletion edit, for EVERY symbol named in the touched files' `use` statements, run a literal search (glob the file, engine: index) for remaining use sites BEFORE the first battery run, and trim every orphaned import in the same edit — one search pass replaces N build cycles. Edit path: anchor-by-read-reference — kill post-compaction re-reads

Symptom (2027-01-14, Mnemo wt/mnemo, job 2c steps 2c.3-2c.5): file_edit requires the EXACT verbatim old_string, so every edit target must have been read in-context; when context compaction drops the verbatim bytes (it keeps summaries, not bytes), every pending edit anchor gets re-read — ~10 re-reads in one afternoon (brain.rs regions, workspace.rs, dispatch approval branch, spawn_agent.rs, policy.rs). Compounding: an oversized read batch auto-archives, and expand_result on it RE-ARCHIVED (the escape hatch failed), forcing fresh small slices instead.

Fix direction: anchor-by-read-reference in the edit tools — read_files already returns line-stamped content per file; give file_edit (and multi_edit's anchor items) an alternative anchor form {from_read: <read-result-id>, lines: [start, end], new_string} validated server-side against the CURRENT file bytes at those lines (any drift = hard fail, forcing a fresh read — never a silent mismatch). The verbatim anchor blob then never needs to live in the model's context; compaction becomes harmless to the edit path. Files: the read tool (src/tool/agent/ files — the read_files implementation), the edit tool (file_edit/multi_edit ops), their schemas. Keep the existing old_string form as-is (default); the reference form is additive.

Acceptance: (1) an edit whose anchor is a line-range reference to a prior read applies cleanly when the file is unchanged; (2) it hard-fails with a clear drift error when the file changed since the read (never a fuzzy apply); (3) a post-compaction session can resume an interrupted edit sequence without re-reading unchanged files; regression tests red-first per constitution; cargo test -p mnemo green.

Memory recall: relevance gate + dismissal feedback + digest integrity

Symptom (2027-01-14, Mnemo wt/mnemo, job 2c session): the auto-recalled memories block injected the SAME five stale rows every turn for ~10 turns (corrupted ".c"-truncated digests from a prior session), each explicitly ignored in reply after reply; later turns injected NEW unrelated rows (optimizer levers 0.70, README six/seven 0.69, an old plan's acceptance criterion 0.70, date-surface quirk 0.78) that matched on generic tokens ("test"/"plan"/"steps"). Cost: repeated context bloat + an ignore-the-noise ritual in every reply; zero recall value for the active work.

Root causes (three, plus one cheap win): (1) recall ranks on the last message alone with no task scoping — the active plan's goal+context (already present in the plan rider) is the better query; (2) no negative feedback — dismissing a row changes nothing for future turns; (3) malformed digests surface forever: ".c"-truncated rows are corrupted at write/index time, and self-contradicted records (e.g. one whose body says "this claim is NO LONGER TRUE") are left live instead of superseded/quarantined; (4) byte-identical recall sets re-inject in full every turn.

Fix direction (src/memory/ + the recall-injection site in prompt assembly): (a) per-session dismissal list — a recall_feedback hook (dismissed record ids) the injector honors for the session's remainder; (b) task-scoped ranking — embed the active plan goal+context alongside the last message so the plan's own records outrank generic 0.7-similarity rows; (c) digest-integrity sweep at index build/startup — quarantine (never delete) records with malformed digests or self-marked no-longer-true bodies; (d) injection dedup — unchanged recall set vs the previous turn injects a one-line sentinel, not the full block.

Acceptance: (1) a dismissed row does not reappear later in the same session; (2) with a plan active, recall ranks the plan's own records above unrelated 0.7-similarity rows; (3) ".c"-truncated digests are quarantined at startup and never injected; (4) an unchanged recall set costs one line; regression tests red-first per constitution; cargo test -p mnemo green.

Pointers: the agent-efficiency series — backlog c439dda0 (search-tool perf), 1ead68c3 (deletion hygiene), 3fdc605f (anchor-by-read-reference); the pending recall-overhaul backlog 4100f5e3 (the big rewrite — this item is its recall-noise half and should be folded or sequenced with it); memory 8d2c2d24 (read_files.rs delta/skeleton work — adjacent, distinct). Tool-argument decode errors: echo received bytes for one-shot recovery

Problem (2027-01-17, wt/mnemo, job 3a.6/3a.8): truncated/malformed tool-call argument payloads (model emission decay — the documented 2026-12-20 bug) reject with bare messages ("ops is required", schema-violation text) that do NOT show what the executor actually received. The agent blind-retries the identical payload, fails identically, and the harness correction loop fires (observed: two identical timeout corrections + repeated "ops is required" rejections on ~2.5-4 KB multi_edit/file_edit payloads; each costs a full round-trip).

Sites (verify first): the tool-argument decode + schema validation producers of "[tool error] ... is required" under src/tool/ and src/agent/dispatch.rs; the malformed-JSON rejection path for arguments. Do NOT regress src/tool/agent/edit_ops.rs:186/:199 — its messages are pinned by tests (backlog 08d2125d's landing; .coding/knowledge/spec/2027-01-11-emission-artifact-guard-per-op-delta-attribution.md).

Fix direction: on any argument decode/schema failure, the error the model sees should carry: (1) the failure kind (JSON parse vs schema field), (2) the byte offset plus a ~120-char received-tail around the break, (3) the named missing/unexpected field, (4) the remedy line (re-emit smaller / chunk / file_write full-file). Add "received N bytes" so truncation is self-evident — never leave a rejection blind-retryable.

Acceptance: unit tests feeding a deliberately truncated arguments JSON (mid-string AND mid-brace) assert the error names offset/tail + missing field; the pinned edit_ops substring tests stay green; full battery (cargo test -p mnemo; --features browser,embeddings; --workspace).

Related: .coding/knowledge/bug/2026-12-20-code-bearing-tool-payload-emissions-degrade-unde.md (root cause), backlog 08d2125d (the landed artifact guard — complementary).

Persistent session context — durable resume without loss

The agent session's CONTEXT (the transcript + the resume-relevant session state) lives in memory only: a shutdown loses the conversation unless the caller exported a transcript themselves. Durable today: plan files (.coding/plans/<id>.md — the crash-resumption doc) and memory_write facts; NOT durable: the conversation and the spawn settings. The resume seam already exists but nothing persists to it — a caller must build `SpawnOptions { resume: Some(Transcript { messages }) }` (src/headless/types.rs) by hand and thread the same model/permissions/limits to reconstruct the session.

Problem to solve: with the option ON, every session durably snapshots at turn boundaries + park/end so ANY point is resumable without loss; with the option OFF, zero new disk writes and today's behavior is byte-identical.

Fix direction:
(1) Config option `persist_context` (default false — behavior-preserving) in the [general] section, src/config/general.rs (follow the compaction_survival pattern around :776), surfaced as a toggle in the GUI options dialog (the Settings pages + the config IPC).
(2) Persistence hook at turn end / park / session end: serialize Transcript + the resume state (model, permissions, limits, host_tools specs, external_policy spec) into the state dir (e.g. <state>/sessions/<session-id>.json) via the existing export machinery — `AgentSession::export_conversation` + `snapshot()` (src/headless/session.rs; §5.9.5 snapshot/pending in .coding/specs/headless-free-agent.md).
(3) An Engine-side restore surface (e.g. `Engine::saved_sessions()` / `Engine::resume_session(id)`) that rebuilds SpawnOptions from the snapshot and spawns with `resume: Some(...)` — the initial_messages threading already exists in spawn_agent_shared (src/host/runtime.rs:73-289).
(4) Multi-platform: pure Rust + the existing config/IPC surfaces — no platform-specific paths (the state dir comes from Workspace.state_dir).

Acceptance criteria:
- Scripted-provider integration test (tests/integration/headless_kernel.rs pattern — RecordingLlm + opts(Workspace, cfg)): with the option on, run a turn, DROP the engine, start a fresh engine on the same state dir, resume the saved session, and assert the model's first request carries the prior messages + the spawn settings round-trip.
- With the option off: no new files appear under the state dir and all existing tests stay green.
- The toggle is visible in the options dialog and takes effect for NEW sessions (documented).
- Full workspace battery green (cargo test, exit 0, zero warnings under #![deny(warnings)]).

Pointers: memory "PLAN: Job 3c resume — D3 mid-step" (the manual state-save pattern this automates); master spec .coding/specs/headless-free-agent.md §5.9.5 + §5.3 (resume); the transcript export (AgentSession::export_conversation) and spawn threading (src/host/runtime.rs:73-289).

Second-instance warning survives shutdown

Problem (user-reported this session; the SECOND live report on this warning — the first, 2027-01-15 "it had switched away", is recorded in SPEC .coding/knowledge/spec/2027-01-11-same-project-instance-warning-is-a-launch-time-s.md): closing mnemo down does not clean up the "another instance of mnemo is running on this project" warning. Repro: (1) launch instance A on a project, launch instance B on the same project (B shows the warning dialog); close A — B's dialog stays on screen, still claiming an instance is working on the project; (2) on clean exit nothing removes <project>/.coding/instance.json, so a stale marker can later warn again when Windows recycles the dead pid to a live process.

Root cause (per the SPEC): <project>/.coding/instance.json {pid, started_at} is written ONLY at launch (src-tauri/src/main.rs:328-344; sole writer InstanceMarker::write src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs:49) — nothing clears or updates it on app exit or project switch-away. The conflict is computed ONCE at startup (conflict_for src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs:69 + instance_pid_alive src-tauri/src/startup.rs:115) -> runtime ctx (src-tauri/src/ipc/state.rs:155) -> StartupSnapshot -> frontend state (frontend/src/App.tsx:261); the dialog (App.tsx:731) renders while non-null, never re-evaluated, never retracted. It warns, does not lock.

Fix direction: (1) src-tauri: on clean exit (app exit + the project-switch restart path src-tauri/src/ipc/projects.rs:201) remove <project>/.coding/instance.json ONLY when the stored marker still names this process (read_marker + pid == std::process::id() guard before delete — last-writer-wins means a newer incumbent must be preserved); best-effort, never block exit; add the removal helper in src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs with unit tests in its mod tests. (2) frontend: re-evaluate the conflict while the dialog is visible (liveness re-check on an interval/focus) and retract once the pid is dead; reword the dialog copy to "launched on this project (PID n, HH:MM)" per the SPEC — never assert current occupancy.

Acceptance: closing the warned-about instance retracts the surviving instance's warning without restart; after a clean exit the marker file is gone when the exiting instance was the last writer; crash re-launch still ignores its own stale marker; cargo test green with the new unit tests.

Related: SPEC .coding/knowledge/spec/2027-01-11-same-project-instance-warning-is-a-launch-time-s.md (mechanism + fix direction), SPEC 2027-01-11-per-instance-webview2-udfs-same-project-conflict.md, plan 5ce69497 (merged 5b18497), review .coding/reviews/2026-09-13-5ce69497-webview-udf-per-instance-review.md (pid-recycling residual).

App unification on the headless Engine (IpcState Engine + console rebuild)

Follow-up job split from headless-free-agent job 5 D5 (the master's stop-split rule, master-spec :770-772; step file .coding/specs/headless-free-agent/job-05-final-acceptance.md §F 5.5). The full §5.9.10 :747-753 item: "the mnemo app is rebuilt on the public API — IpcState holds an Engine; every IPC command + the console REPL go through Engine/AgentSession/Setup/*Api".

PROBLEM / WHY IT SPLIT: two blockers found by the D5 probe (2026-10-13, tree 5d97bc1): (1) `Engine::brain()` is pub(crate) (src/headless/engine.rs:138) — an Engine constructed app-side builds its OWN brain, so "IpcState holds an Engine" as specced forks the app into two brain halves sharing only the memory store (the D7 `.memory_store(Arc<dyn MemoryStoreTrait>)` seam, engine.rs:113); doing it right needs a NEW design decision — either a pub brain-injection seam on EngineBuilder (mirroring .memory_store/.shared_resources) or a deliberate two-lane architecture doc. (2) console.rs is 2,733 lines with its own AgentManager/AgentLoopFactory/HostRuntime loop wiring (:33-41, :1180, :1216, :1497-1501) — the rebuild alone exceeds the ~3k-line split threshold.

EXACT SEAMS (probed, verified 2026-10-13): the GUI Ready branch builds the brain at src-tauri/src/main.rs:393 (build_brain) with the handles at :459-474 (brain.own_memory_store: Option<Arc<MemoryStore>> — the concrete store for the .memory_store coercion; brain.workspace.root; the brain.config tokio-Mutex Arc — NOT reachable from an Engine today; block_on precedent at :462); the console path builds its own at console.rs:1180. create_plan UX: cut the two first-call failure modes (steps-as-string, gate evidence phrasing)

Problem (2027-01-15, dispatching backlog c439dda0 -> plan 89bbd2a9): two consecutive create_plan rejections before the plan landed — each costs a full re-emit of a multi-KB call and a recovery round.

(1) steps-as-string: the `steps` argument went out as a JSON-encoded STRING instead of a native array. The error ("an argument must be a sequence, not a string. Please check each parameter's type against the tool's schema", rendered at src/tool/error_message.rs:87) names NEITHER the offending parameter NOR the expected shape — the agent must guess. The steps property doc (src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:700-709) says "array" but never warns against the string form, while the content-first flow (write the plan in the reply first, then emit the call) primes pasting the drafted JSON as a string. Repro: emit create_plan with steps as a string containing the JSON array.

(2) resumability-gate evidence phrasing: a context whose findings all came from fresh file reads was rejected at context line 4 ("- Engine choice: src/tool/agent/search.rs:1659 - index path only under ...") as "asserts a symbol is callable/reachable without evidence". The gate (src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:499; tests :2865, :3890) pattern-matches per-line evidence words (verified/probe/probed/observed/measured/confirmed/reproduced/checked) or an 'assumption:' label. The context property (src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:699) lists the words but never states the OPERATIONAL convention: the evidence word must open the SAME line as the claim, e.g. "verified (read src/x.rs:12-40): ..." — so plainly-phrased, genuinely-evidenced findings fail on call one.

Assessment (user asked: too strict or weak instructions?): weak instructions in both spots. The gate's strictness is deliberate and right (SPEC cb44db42, fail-closed against thin plans) — keep it; failure 1 is a typing trap with an error too generic to recover from quickly.

Fix direction: (a) src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs steps property (:700-709): add "steps MUST be a native JSON array — never a string containing JSON"; (b) context property (:699): add the per-line phrasing convention + one passing example bullet ("verified (read src/x.rs:12-40): ..."); (c) src/tool/error_message.rs:87: thread the failing parameter name + expected shape into the type error ("steps: expected array, got string; emit [{\"header\":..., \"body\":...}]") — the schema-validation layer must pass the property name through; (d) optional lenient shim: `steps` arriving as a string that parses as a valid steps JSON array is accepted with a NOTE instead of an error; (e) optionally evaluate gate-side recognition of read-anchored findings without magic words — if not feasible, (a)-(c) alone carry the fix; keep the gate fail-closed either way.

Acceptance: (1) steps-as-string either succeeds via the shim (with note) or errors naming `steps` + the expected shape; (2) a context whose claim lines open with "verified (read ...):" passes the gate first try; (3) an unevidenced "X is reachable from Y" line is still rejected (fail-closed pinned by gate tests at src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:2865/:3890); (4) regression tests for the shim + the description texts (mirror the schema_advertises_* assertion pattern, e.g. src/tool/agent/search.rs:1903); (5) cargo test --workspace green.

Remove the LiteLLM proxy-cache ceiling from compaction triggering

Problem / decision (2027-01-25, user decision): the compaction trigger is computed as `min(fill_rate x window, ceiling - 32_768)` by `ContextManager::effective_summarize_threshold` (src/agent/context.rs:407-419, reached via `effective_summarize_at` at src/agent/context.rs:301). The `proxy_cache_ceiling_tokens` dial (default Some(340_000), src/config/general.rs:957) exists to keep requests under the ~340K-token cliff where LiteLLM-class proxies drop whole-conversation prefix caching (hit rate ~99% -> ~4%). Analysis: with the default fill rate 0.3 the ceiling only binds on windows > ~1.02M tokens (0.3 x 1_024_000 > 307_232); on every smaller window the fill-rate product fires first, LiteLLM or not. The cap is therefore a second, rarely-binding, hard-coded override of the user's actual dial. DECISION: remove the ceiling cap entirely — the trigger respects ONLY the config dial `summarize_at_fill_rate` (default 0.3, src/config/general.rs:954). A user on a LiteLLM proxy who wants the old behavior sets the dial themselves (0.3 on a 1M window = 300K, under the cliff).

Fix direction (files + symbols):
- src/agent/context.rs: `effective_summarize_threshold(max_tokens, fill_rate, ceiling)` — drop the `ceiling` param and the `min` cap; `effective_summarize_at` (:301) stops passing it; remove the `proxy_cache_ceiling` field (:124, :136-141), the `with_proxy_cache_ceiling` builder (:280-283), the `proxy_cache_ceiling()` accessor (:421-424), and cliff-mentioning doc comments (:57-62, :126-141, :275-300).

- src/config/general.rs: remove `proxy_cache_ceiling_tokens` from ContextConfig (:943-948) and its default (:957); update the struct doc (:921-924).
- src/config/settings_dto.rs: remove the patch field, its validation (~:465), the apply site (~:769), and any test fixtures (~:986).
- src/config/mod.rs / src/config/general.rs: update config-example round-trip tests that mention the key.

- src/agent/turn.rs:664-666 — the run_turn comment block describing the proxy-cache trigger — update.
- src/agent/context.rs tests (~:2411-:2600, the raise-cap/ceiling interplay tests; any test asserting the ceiling caps the trigger) — rework to the fill-rate-only formula.

Acceptance criteria:

The ops path refuses too: "r113:} produced no change — the payload equals the replaced line(s)". (c) read_files rejects a stringified files array ("an argument must be a sequence, not a string") even when the string parses as a JSON array — hit 3x in one turn (two identical re-emissions needed harness correction).

1. The file-edit engine (search "no-op edit" / "payload equals the replaced line" — likely src/tool/agent/file_edit.rs or its shared editor module): make the old/new comparison byte-exact — do NOT strip a trailing newline from new_string — and make the splice WRITE preserve the final newline. Streamed answer stays plain until the next LLM request

Problem (user-reported live this session, late Jan 2027, watching a streaming answer): the assistant's answer renders as plain text (no markdown) while it streams AND stays plain after the turn completes — headings/lists/code fences apply only once the next request is sent. Repro: ask for a markdown answer (list or code fence); it streams plain; the turn finishes — still plain; send the next prompt — now it is formatted.

Verified mechanism (recon this session, branch wt/mnemo):
- Plain-while-streaming is DELIBERATE: frontend/src/components/chat/Message.tsx:278-291 — MessageImpl's `assistant` case renders raw text while the `streaming` prop is set ("avoid re-parsing markdown on every token"); full markdown (frontend/src/components/chat/Markdown.tsx → lazy MarkdownImpl.tsx, react-markdown) renders only once the entry sits in the transcript WITHOUT `streaming`.
- frontend/src/components/chat/Conversation.tsx:217-222 + 285: while state.streamingText is non-empty a streamingBlock renders that text with `streaming`; it unmounts once flushStreamingText clears the field.
- The turn-end flush DOES exist: frontend/src/hooks/agentEventReducer.ts:1373-1399 reduceFinished calls flushStreamingText (line 1384; reduceError:1437 too); flushStreamingText (frontend/src/hooks/agentState.ts:679-686) pushes the text into the transcript and clears streamingText.

Root-cause suspects (both fit the symptom — untangle which is live):
(a) rAF delta-buffer ordering race: text deltas are buffered and appended per rAF frame (frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStore.ts:560 + :1155; frontend/src/hooks/deltaFlush.ts). A buffered flush landing AFTER the finished event ran flushStreamingText re-populates streamingText → the plain streamingBlock re-mounts and lingers until the next request; reduceStarted (agentEventReducer.ts:200-204) then clears streamingText WITHOUT flushing, dropping that tail.
(b) The activity-log mirror: the answer is also mirrored into activityLog as `answer` entries (appendAnswerEntry, agentEventReducer.ts:257-268, called from reduceTextDelta:283) and the log is NOT cleared at flush (agentState.ts:668-677 — "stays visible until new reasoning starts"), so the thinking box keeps showing the PLAIN answer after the turn ends; check how the reasoning box / InflightBar renders `answer` entries — that may be the copy the user perceives as "still not formatted".

Fix direction: at turn end the answer must render as markdown in the transcript immediately, with no plain remnant in the chat or the thinking box — either drain the rAF buffer before/into the finished flush, or make late deltas not resurrect streamingText after the turn; and/or render the settled answer mirror as markdown once the turn is over (decide per root cause). Keep the per-token plain-text streaming render (a deliberate perf choice); live markdown DURING streaming is a separate optional enhancement.

Acceptance: (1) after a turn finishes the full answer renders markdown with no user action and no plain remnant; (2) text followed by a tool call still flushes ABOVE the tool card (existing contract, agentState.ts:674-677); (3) regression test via the reducer harness (useAgentStore.test.ts pattern): dispatch text_delta(s) → finished with fake timers, including a delta flush landing AFTER finished; assert streamingText === "" AND the transcript's last entry is the full assistant text (must be red before the fix); (4) npm test in frontend/ green.
